title: Galaxies and Asteroids
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Science 0893 · Stage 8 · Earth and Space
summary: What a galaxy is made of — stars, planetary systems, dust and gas — and how asteroids formed from rocks left over when the Solar System formed, with diagrams, worked examples and a Checkpoint-style quiz.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Describe a galaxy: a huge group of stars and planetary systems, with clouds of dust and gas between them (stellar dust and gas). (8ESs.01)
Describe asteroids as rocks that are smaller than planets, and explain that they formed from rocks left over when a planetary system formed. (8ESs.02)

blocks.text: 1. Key words

items: star
نجم — a huge ball of hot gas that gives out its own light, like the Sun
planet
كوكب — a large, round object that orbits a star and does not give out its own light
orbit
مدار / يدور حول — the path of one object around another
planetary system
نظام كوكبي — a star and all the planets and smaller objects that orbit it
Solar System
المجموعة الشمسية — our planetary system: the Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets
galaxy
مجرة — a huge group of stars, planetary systems, dust and gas held together by gravity
the Milky Way
درب التبانة — the galaxy we live in
stellar dust
غبار نجمي — tiny solid grains floating between the stars
nebula (plural nebulae)
سديم — a cloud of dust and gas in space where new stars form
gravity
الجاذبية — the force of attraction between all objects with mass
asteroid
كويكب — a rocky object, smaller than a planet, that orbits the Sun
asteroid belt
حزام الكويكبات — the region between Mars and Jupiter where most asteroids orbit
Universe
الكون — everything that exists: all the galaxies and the space between them

blocks.text: 2. What is a galaxy?
A **galaxy** is an enormous group of **stars**, **planetary systems** and clouds of **dust and gas**, all held together by **gravity**. Our Sun is just one star in a galaxy called the **Milky Way**.

rows: Huge balls of hot gas that give out light. A galaxy can have millions to hundreds of billions of stars. The Milky Way has more than 100 billion.
Many stars have planets and other objects orbiting them. Our planetary system is the Solar System. Astronomers have already found more than 6000 planets orbiting other stars.
Tiny solid grains (a bit like soot and very fine sand) spread between the stars.
Mostly **hydrogen** and **helium**. Where dust and gas gather into big clouds (**nebulae**), gravity can pull them together to make **new stars and planets**.

blocks.title: A full-mark description of a galaxy
blocks.text: A galaxy is a very large group of **stars** and their **planetary systems**, with **dust and gas** between them, held together by **gravity**.
3. Our galaxy — the Milky Way

The Milky Way is a **spiral galaxy**: from above it would look like a flat, spinning disc with a bulge of stars in the centre and long curved **spiral arms**. The arms are full of stars, dust and gas. The Sun is in one of the arms, about halfway from the centre to the edge.

blocks.caption: A model of the Milky Way seen from above. We can never see it like this, because we are inside it.

items: The Milky Way is about **100 000 light-years** across. A **light-year** is the distance light travels in one year — about 9.5 million million km. Light is the fastest thing there is, yet it would take 100 000 years to cross our galaxy.
The Sun takes about 230 million years to travel once around the centre of the galaxy.

On a very dark night, far from city lights (for example in the Western Desert or Sinai), you can see the Milky Way as a pale band of light across the sky. That band is the light of billions of distant stars in the disc of our galaxy, seen from the inside.
The dark patches in the band are clouds of **dust** blocking the light of the stars behind them.

blocks.alt: The Milky Way as a bright arch of stars across a dark night sky
blocks.caption: The Milky Way seen from a dark desert in Chile: the bright band is the disc of our galaxy, with dark dust clouds; the two small smudges on the left are the Magellanic Clouds.
blocks.credit: Photo: Bruno Gilli/ESO / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

blocks.text: **Other galaxies:** the Universe contains at least hundreds of billions of galaxies. They have different shapes:

rows: Flat disc with spiral arms and a central bulge
The Milky Way; the Andromeda Galaxy (about 2.5 million light-years away)
Smooth, oval or round ball of stars, with little dust and gas
The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, small galaxies near the Milky Way

blocks.alt: The Andromeda Galaxy, a large spiral galaxy seen at an angle
blocks.caption: The Andromeda Galaxy, a spiral galaxy about 2.5 million light-years away; the light from it left about 2.5 million years ago.
blocks.credit: Photo: Adam Evans / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

blocks.title: المجرة يعني إيه؟
blocks.text: **المجرة** = مجموعة ضخمة جدًا من **النجوم** و**الأنظمة الكوكبية** (نجم وحواليه كواكب) و**غبار وغاز** بين النجوم، وكلهم مربوطين ببعض بـ**الجاذبية**. إحنا عايشين في مجرة اسمها **درب التبانة**، والشمس نجم واحد بس من أكتر من ١٠٠ مليار نجم فيها. الترتيب من الأصغر: كوكب ← نجم ← نظام كوكبي ← مجرة ← الكون.
4. What is an asteroid?

An **asteroid** is a lump of **rock** (some also contain a lot of metal, such as iron and nickel) that orbits the Sun. Asteroids are **much smaller than planets**. Most are not round: they are lumpy, like potatoes, because their gravity is too weak to pull them into a ball.

rows: Ceres (the largest; now also called a dwarf planet)

blocks.alt: The cratered, lumpy surface of the asteroid Vesta
blocks.caption: Vesta, about 525 km across, photographed by NASA's Dawn spacecraft: it is cratered and not perfectly round.
blocks.credit: Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UCLA/MPS/DLR/IDA / Wikimedia Commons, public domain

blocks.text: Compare these with the Earth, which is about 12 700 km across. Even all the asteroids in the asteroid belt put together have only a few per cent of the mass of our Moon.

items: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in the **asteroid belt**, between the orbits of **Mars** and **Jupiter**. There are more than a million asteroids bigger than 1 km there.
In films the asteroid belt is crowded, but really the asteroids are very far apart — spacecraft have flown through it without hitting anything.

Some asteroids have orbits that come close to the Earth. About 66 million years ago an asteroid roughly 10 km wide hit the Earth, and scientists link it to the extinction of the dinosaurs. Today astronomers track near-Earth asteroids, and in 2022 a spacecraft (the DART mission) crashed into a small asteroid and changed its orbit.

blocks.caption: Most asteroids orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter, in the asteroid belt. (Mercury, Venus and the planets beyond Jupiter are not shown.)

rows: Rock (and metal) orbiting the Sun, smaller than a planet
A lump of **ice and dust**; it grows a glowing tail when it comes close to the Sun
Comets are icy, asteroids are rocky
The streak of light ("shooting star") made when a small piece of rock burns up in the Earth's atmosphere
A meteor is the light, not the rock
A piece of space rock that lands on the Earth's surface
Many meteorites are small pieces of asteroids

blocks.text: 5. How asteroids formed
To understand asteroids, look at how a planetary system such as the Solar System forms. Scientists think this happened about **4.6 billion years ago**:

items: A huge cloud of **dust and gas** (a nebula) in the galaxy began to collapse because of **gravity**.
As it shrank, it began to spin and flattened into a **disc**.
Most of the material was pulled to the centre and became hot enough to form a **star** — the Sun.
In the disc, dust grains stuck together to make small rocks; rocks crashed together and joined to make bigger rocks; the biggest pulled in more material by gravity and grew into **planets**.
**Not all the rocks became part of a planet.** The rocks **left over** are the **asteroids**.

Between Mars and Jupiter, the very strong gravity of the giant planet **Jupiter** kept stirring the rocks up, so they crashed and broke instead of joining together. That is why there is an asteroid belt there instead of another planet.

blocks.text: Because asteroids have hardly changed since then, they are like **time capsules**. Spacecraft from Japan and the USA have collected tiny samples from asteroids and brought them back to the Earth to learn what the early Solar System was made of.

blocks.alt: The asteroid Bennu, a dark grey rocky body covered in boulders
blocks.caption: The small asteroid Bennu, photographed by NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft, which brought a sample of its rock back to the Earth in 2023.
blocks.credit: Photo: NASA/Goddard/University of Arizona / Wikimedia Commons, public domain

blocks.title: الكويكب يعني إيه؟
blocks.text: **الكويكب** = صخرة (وأحيانًا فيها معادن) بتدور حوالين الشمس، و**أصغر بكتير من الكواكب**. أغلب الكويكبات في **حزام الكويكبات** بين **المريخ** و**المشتري**. اتكونت من **الصخور اللي فضلت** بعد ما الكواكب اتكونت من سحابة الغبار والغاز، وجاذبية المشتري منعتها تتجمع وتعمل كوكب.
6. Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Describe what a galaxy is made of. [3]

items: Stars (1).
Planetary systems / planets orbiting stars (1).
Dust and gas (clouds of stellar dust and gas) (1).
Extra detail that helps: they are all held together by **gravity**.
**Common mistake:** "a galaxy is a group of planets". Planets are only part of it — the main things are **stars**, plus dust and gas.

blocks.text: **Worked example 2** — Write these in order of size, starting with the smallest: **galaxy, planet, Universe, star, planetary system**. [2]

items: Think about what is inside what: a planet orbits a star; a star with its planets is a planetary system; billions of these make a galaxy; all the galaxies are in the Universe.
Answer: **planet → star → planetary system → galaxy → Universe** (2 marks; 1 mark if only one pair is swapped).
**Common mistake:** putting the Solar System before the Sun. The Solar System *contains* the Sun, so it is bigger.

blocks.text: **Worked example 3** — Give **two** ways in which asteroids are different from planets. [2]

items: Any two: asteroids are much **smaller** (1); most are **not round** / irregular in shape (1); there are millions of asteroids but only eight planets (1); most asteroids orbit together in a belt, but each planet has its own orbit (1).
**Exam tip:** "Asteroids are rocks" is not a difference by itself — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are rocky too. Say **smaller**.

blocks.text: **Worked example 4** — Describe how the asteroids in the asteroid belt formed. [3]

items: The Solar System formed from a cloud of dust and gas; the dust stuck together to make rocks (1).
Most rocks joined together to make planets, but some were **left over** — these are the asteroids (1).
Between Mars and Jupiter, **Jupiter's gravity** stopped the rocks from joining to form a planet (1).
**Common mistake:** "asteroids are pieces of a planet that exploded". There is no evidence for this; they are left-over building material.

blocks.text: **Worked example 5** — The Earth's diameter is about 12 700 km. Vesta's diameter is about 525 km. How many times wider is the Earth than Vesta? Give your answer to the nearest whole number. [2]

items: This shows why asteroids are described as **much smaller than planets**.

blocks.text: **Worked example 6** — A teacher says: "The Milky Way is like a huge city. Each house is a planetary system, and the people in the house are the star and its planets." (a) Give one way the analogy is useful. [1] (b) Give one way it is **not** like a real galaxy. [1]

items: (a) It shows that a galaxy is made of a very large number of planetary systems grouped together / that a planetary system is a small part of the galaxy (1).

(b) Any one: a city has no clouds of dust and gas between the houses / a galaxy is held together by gravity, a city is not / the planetary systems in a galaxy are extremely far apart compared with houses (1).
**Exam tip:** an analogy is a model. For a strength say what it **shows correctly**; for a weakness say what is **different in the real thing**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Mixing up **galaxy** and **Solar System**. The Solar System is one star and its planets; a galaxy has billions of stars.
Describing a galaxy as "a group of planets". Always name **stars**, **planetary systems**, and **dust and gas**.
Saying asteroids are in a belt between **Earth and Mars**. The asteroid belt is between **Mars and Jupiter**.
Mixing up asteroids (rock) and **comets** (ice and dust with a tail).
Saying asteroids came from a planet that broke apart. They are rocks **left over** from when the planets formed.
Giving a difference that is not a difference: "asteroids are made of rock" (so are the rocky planets). Say **smaller** or **irregular shape**.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: **Describe** a galaxy (2–3 marks): one mark for each correct part — stars, planetary systems, dust and gas.
**Order** objects by size, or **match** words (star, planet, galaxy, asteroid) to descriptions with lines.
**Label a diagram** of the Solar System: where is the asteroid belt?
**Explain** how asteroids formed — use the words **left over** and **formation of the Solar System / planetary system**.
**Use data** in a table (diameters, distances) to compare asteroids with planets — calculator allowed, show working.
**Analogies and models** (8TWSm.01): give a strength and a limitation of a model of a galaxy or of the Solar System.

blocks.text: Practice

blocks.title: Galaxies and asteroids — practice
blocks.intro: Answer every part. Type short answers in the box; for longer answers write yours on paper, then mark it with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Which is the best description of a galaxy?
c: One star with planets orbiting it
A huge group of stars, planetary systems, dust and gas held together by gravity
The empty space between the planets
A ball of ice and dust with a long tail
questions.e: A galaxy contains **stars**, **planetary systems** and **dust and gas**, held together by gravity. One star with its planets is a planetary system; a ball of ice and dust with a tail is a comet.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Solar System?
questions.e: We live in the **Milky Way**, a spiral galaxy. The Sun is in one of its spiral arms.

questions.q: Which list is in order of size, from **smallest** to **largest**?
questions.e: A planet is smaller than its star; a star plus its planets makes a planetary system; billions of these make a galaxy: **planet, star, planetary system, galaxy**.

questions.p:
Question 4
The diagram shows part of the Solar System. It is not drawn to scale.
questions.q: (a) Which letter shows the asteroid belt?
questions.e: **C** is in the region full of small rocks between the orbit of Mars (B) and the orbit of Jupiter (D). A is the Earth.

questions.p:
Question 4
The diagram shows part of the Solar System. It is not drawn to scale.
questions.e: D is the large planet just outside the asteroid belt: **Jupiter**. (A is the Earth and B is Mars.)

questions.q: What are asteroids mainly made of?
c: rock (some contain a lot of metal)
ice, with a tail of dust
questions.e: Asteroids are **rocky** objects; some also contain metals such as iron and nickel. Icy objects with tails are comets; burning gas describes stars.

questions.q: Where did the asteroids in the asteroid belt come from?
c: Pieces knocked off the Earth by volcanoes
Rocks left over from when the planets of the Solar System formed
Old stars that cooled down and became solid
questions.e: Asteroids are **rocks left over from the formation of the Solar System** — material that never became part of a planet.

questions.q: The gas in the clouds between the stars in a galaxy is mostly two gases. One is helium. Name the other.
questions.e: The gas between the stars is mostly **hydrogen**, with helium. Gravity can pull these clouds of gas and dust together to form new stars.

questions.q: Ceres is the largest asteroid. Its diameter is about 940 km. The Earth's diameter is about 12 740 km. How many times wider is the Earth than Ceres? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.e: 12 740 ÷ 940 (1) = 13.55… → **14** to the nearest whole number (1). Even the largest asteroid is tiny compared with a planet.

questions.q: The inner edge of the asteroid belt is about 330 million km from the Sun. The outer edge is about 480 million km from the Sun. How wide is the asteroid belt, in millions of km?

questions.ms: 1 mark: (very large number of) stars. 1 mark: planetary systems / planets orbiting stars. 1 mark: (stellar) dust and gas / nebulae. Accept 'held together by gravity' as a third mark only if one of the other points is missing. Do not accept: 'a group of planets' on its own.
questions.e: A galaxy is a huge group of **stars** (1) and their **planetary systems** (1), with clouds of **dust and gas** between them (1), all held together by gravity.

questions.q: Explain how the asteroids in the asteroid belt formed. [3]
questions.ms: 1 mark: the planetary system / Solar System formed from a cloud of dust and gas, and rocks formed from it. 1 mark: most rocks joined together to make the planets. 1 mark: some rocks were left over and did not join to make a planet — these are the asteroids (accept: rocks left over between Mars and Jupiter). Do not accept: 'from a planet that exploded'.
questions.e: When the Solar System formed, dust in the spinning cloud stuck together to make rocks (1). Most rocks joined to form planets, but some were **left over** — these are the asteroids (1). Between Mars and Jupiter, **Jupiter's strong gravity** stopped them joining to make another planet (1).

questions.q: Scientists say that studying asteroids helps them to learn what the early Solar System was like. Explain why. [2]
questions.ms: 1 mark: asteroids are rocks left over from when the Solar System / planets formed. 1 mark: they have hardly changed since then (unlike the surface of the Earth), so they show what the original material was made of. Accept: 'they are like time capsules' with an explanation.
questions.e: Asteroids are **left over from the formation of the Solar System** (1). They have changed very little in 4.6 billion years, so they still show what the **original building material** of the planets was made of (1).
Most asteroids are less than 1 km across. The Sun is a star, the Solar System contains the Sun, and the Milky Way contains billions of stars — so **a typical asteroid** is the smallest.

blocks.title: Remember
items: A **galaxy** is a huge group of **stars**, **planetary systems** and **dust and gas**, held together by gravity.
We live in the **Milky Way**, a spiral galaxy; the Sun is one star in one of its arms.
Order of size: planet → star → planetary system → galaxy → Universe.
**Asteroids** are rocks (some with metal), **smaller than planets**, orbiting the Sun — most in the **asteroid belt** between **Mars and Jupiter**.
Asteroids are rocks **left over from the formation of the Solar System**; Jupiter's gravity stopped them from forming a planet.
